newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Long Australian bond yields up, market supported.
newsitem.headline: Long Australian bond yields up, market supported.

text.p: *Long-dated Australian bond yields rose slightly as the market drew breath after Friday's post-rate cut rally, meandering in a narrow range for most of the day.
Long-dated Australian bond yields rose slightly as the market drew breath after Friday's post-rate cut rally, meandering in a narrow range for most of the day.

However, traders said the market was holding up well given the heavy profit-taking that was seen after yields struck four month lows on Friday on the policy easing, which was continued by offshore investors in after hours trading.

"We are hearing that a lot of people are interested in the market now, which is strange given that yields are still well below levels seen before the rate cut. It could be that they see the authorities are concerned about growth," one trader said.
The absence of trading in U.S. Treasuries in Asia due to the U.S. Memorial Day holiday also lent to a quieter session. U.K. markets are also closed.

The local market sees a barrage of data this week, starting with first quarter capital expenditure on Tuesday, although these are somewhat overshadowed with the rate cut already in place, traders said.
The U.S. market sees a slim data calender this week, but does face two notes auctions with US$16.5 billion of two-year paper on Wednesday and a US$12 billion five-year sale on Thursday.
Local yield differentials to the dollar bloc showed only minor movements, but the long end gave up some ground to the U.S. after Friday's sharp post-rate cut spread tightening.
The local yield curve continued to steepen following the policy easing, putting on some 15 b.p. in the past two days.
